title: Text Alignment
definition: Utilities for controlling the alignment of text.
simpleExplanation: Controlling whether text sticks to the left, right, or center of its container.
realWorldExample: Using `text-center` on a pricing page header, but leaving the actual pricing features as `text-left` so they are easy to read in a list.

intermediate: If you apply `text-center` to a `<span class="inline">`, why doesn't the text actually center on the page?

answers.question: Why span doesn't center?
answers.answer: Because an `inline` element perfectly shrinks to the width of its text. There is no empty space *inside* the span for the text to move around in. Text alignment only works on block-level containers.

codeExample:
I stick to the left (Default for English).

I am perfectly in the middle.

I stick to the right (Great for currency amounts!).

I will stretch the spaces between my words so that I create a perfectly flush square block of text on both the left AND the right sides, just like a newspaper column.
